How the app uses these limits

The app checks every logged air test against these limits and shows a red notice when one is outside them. A blank field uses the standard value in its label — it never turns the app’s check off. Enter your own only where your program or this space calls for different limits, and keep using your gas meter’s own alarm too. H2S and CO are checked on the tests where they are measured; a blank reading means not measured, never zero.
Maximum acceptable O2 (%) — blank uses 23.5 (oxygen-enriched air is a fire hazard)
Maximum H2S (ppm) — blank uses 10 ppm, the OSHA construction limit (8-hour average)
Maximum CO (ppm) — blank uses 25 ppm, the Cal/OSHA limit (stricter than NIOSH’s 35 and federal OSHA’s 50)
Air test re-check reminder (minutes, optional — blank = Off)
A reminder to log a fresh test, not a gas limit. It also sets how old the last test can be before check-in is blocked (20 min when blank). Blank means no reminder, never 0 minutes.

<1>2. Station (required)</1><2>0+00.00 L 20.00</2>: station 0+00.00, 20.00 ft left of the line. 1+50 or 150.00 both mean 150 ft. The side and offset are optional. A row with only a point number instead of a station is listed but can’t be a run point.

<1>3. Description (optional)</1><2>20/SD CL CB #4 TG</2>. “20/SD” is a 20 ft offset to the storm drain, not a pipe size. Rows like this one (TG, rim, FG, TC, BM, L/O) are listed but not pre-checked as pipe points.
<1>4. Plan elevation (required)</1><2>2394.00</2>. Checked, not imported: stake elevation minus the cut must match it within 0.01 ft.
<1>5. Cut/Fill (required)</1><2>C-6.09</2>: cut 6.09 ft. C is always down and F always up; a + or − after the letter doesn’t change that.
<1>6. Stake elevation (required)</1><2>2400.09</2>. The invert imported is stake elevation − cut (or + fill): 2400.09 − 6.09 = 2394.00.
<1>7–8. Northing, Easting (required, not imported)</1><2>2291289.61 6381670.85</2>. They end the row.

Limits: numbers need a decimal point (2394.00, not 2394); feet-inches values aren’t read; spaces or tabs between columns both work, and thousands commas are fine in the number columns. A line the app can’t read is listed under “couldn’t be read”, never guessed. More in Education: Reading Stationing & Cutsheets.
